newsitem.title: CANADA: Rand decline has yet to lift SAA exports to US.
newsitem.headline: Rand decline has yet to lift SAA exports to US.

text.p: South African Airways has yet to see a major increase in cargo traffic to the U.S. despite an almost 20 percent depreciation the rand, says a senior SAA Cargo official.
SAA's U.S. export traffic to South Africa remains a lot stronger than import traffic from South Africa, Clive Langeveldt, cargo manager for the Americas, said in an interview from New York.
Ex-U.S.demand remains solid enough to fill almost 300 tonnes of freighter and bellyhold capacity each week.

"This (imbalance) is a bit disappointing because we would like to have seen South African manufacturers take more advantage of the weak rand-dollar exchange rate to promote their goods" in North America.
"We are anticipating an increase towards the end of the year," he said.
So far, it seems that South Africa exporters have focused on traditional customers in Europe and Asia, he said.
Northbound from Johannesburg, the freighters are routed through Amsterdam, then on to New York. They leave South Africa full of goods for Europe and rarely carry SAA freight to the U.S.
Between Amsterdam and New York, the flight is chartered by a third party.

During the summer, the southbound flights were shared with Amsterdam. The result was space shortages for SAA New York. On some flights, as much as 20-40 tonnes of tendered cargo could not be accommodated, said Langeveldt.
For the fall, the freighters will operate as a direct service southbound from New York to Johannesburg.
